title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% Wednesday in a 10-2 vote; Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of a hike, and Chair Warsh said politics played 'no role' ahead of midterms — odds of a December hike are rising.

Markets: Thursday's close was mixed/lower — Nasdaq fell ~1.4% and the S&P 500 slipped as Alphabet sank on AI-spending and search-growth worries, even as most individual stocks rose and Microsoft held up better on ~43% Azure growth.

Macro/Policy: The advance Q3 GDP estimate (released Thursday) showed the strongest quarterly growth in about two years, driven by consumer spending, though economists flagged slowing momentum heading into Q4.

Companies: Amazon missed on EPS ($1.89) and revenue (~$201.9B) despite AWS surging 39% to ~$46B and a record 13.9% operating margin; soft Q4 revenue guidance ($240B-$247B) and ~$77B of quarterly capex sent shares down 6-7% after hours.

Companies: Mastercard beat estimates (adjusted EPS $5.31, revenue +14% to $9.8B) on resilient consumer spending; Caterpillar posted a big beat (sales +17% to $20.7B, adjusted EPS $7.20) on record backlog and AI-driven power demand, though shares still weighed on the Dow.
Companies: Today's slate includes Chevron and AbbVie before the open and Apple after the close, capping one of the busiest weeks of the Q3 earnings season.
